doc.title: Bley Carla — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Not writing, playing naive piano and the Phase Two gigs
summary: She had stopped composing and played piano ignorantly, but led Saturday gigs at the Phase Two coffee house with Haden, Swallow, Rudd and Lacy playing Monk tunes.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: So were you... so you were experiencing all this incredible music. Were you still engaged in writing at the time? You were composing?

No, no. Nothing. I stopped writing music when I was maybe ten, or eight, because I thought life was better. I want to live life and not sit in a room. Now I want to sit in a room, but then I didn’t and I didn’t sit in a room until Paul Bley made me write music.
Ok. And piano wise you also just stopped playing piano?

No. Well I stopped playing piano. I played piano a little bit, but I played really, really, with total ignorance of how to play the piano. That I didn’t learn until I got together with Steve Swallow. I just played stupid stuff. A very stupid style. I don’t have any recordings from then so you wouldn’t believe how awful it was, cause it wasn’t recorded. But I would play Monk tunes, but, probably, ahh I wouldn’t have played them wrong, but I’d think I’d play the tune but I didn’t know how to solo on it. I would, I had a gig at the Phase Two every Saturday, it was a coffee house, and I had the band and I would hire people to play with me. Well anytime anybody needed five dollars they’d come down and work with me for the afternoon. And I got a lot of really great people down there, a lot of good bass players, Charley Haden, Steve Swallow, Roswell Rudd and Steve Lacy playing Monk tunes, that’s where I learned all the Monk tunes, but I didn’t solo on them or anything, I didn’t know how to improvise. I really didn’t. I couldn’t make anything up. I could just arrange it. If I were gonna play a tune I would just sit down and arrange it. But that was a long time ago. And I can’t remember what the next thing is.
